claim: For every L-site open hard-core chain with K_L=J sum_{i=0}^L (b_{i+1}-b_i)^*(b_{i+1}-b_i), b_0=b_{L+1}=0, J in [J_-,J_+], tau in [tau_-,tau_+] with J_-,tau_->0, |lambda|<=B, beta=tau L^2, and W_L=sum_{nonempty X:diam(X)<=R} V_X prod_{i in X}n_i with V_X>=0 and fixed finite R, the normalized Gibbs state of K_L+W_L-lambda M/L^2 obeys Pr(M>=d)<=C_geo exp[-(4/3)tau J d^3+C_2 d^2] for every 1<=d<=L, with constants depending only on the public compact ranges and not on L,R, or W. For d>L the tail is zero.
assumptions: Open hard-core path with shifted Dirichlet Laplacian normalization and positive J.
W is finite, positive semidefinite, and number preserving; the stated density form with V_X>=0 suffices. Empty-set scalar terms are removed.
beta=tau L^2; the field term is -lambda M/L^2 in the Hamiltonian, so its Gibbs factor is exp(tau lambda M).
tau,J lie in fixed compact subsets bounded away from zero and |lambda|<=B.
proof: Within each M sector W>=0 implies ordered eigenvalues of K+W dominate K by min-max, hence Z_M(W)<=Z_M(0), without assuming [K,W]=0. The vacuum has weight one in the full partition function. Jordan-Wigner and the open sine transform give e_k=4J sin^2(pi k/(2(L+1))); sin x>=2x/pi gives e_k>=4Jk^2/(L+1)^2. Distinct occupied modes and k_i=i+s_i yield Z_M(0)<=exp[-a_L sum_{i<=M}i^2](1-exp[-2a_*])^{-M}, where a_L=4tau J L^2/(L+1)^2>=a_*=tau_-J_-; a geometric sum over M>=d gives the stated cubic exponent and finite-size O(d^2) correction. Full derivation is derivation.txt.
explicit_constants: Let a_*=tau_-J_-, C_*=tau_+B-log(1-exp(-2a_*)). Choose integer d_*>=1 with a_*(d_*+1)^2>=C_*+a_*/2; C_geo=(1-exp(-a_*/2))^-1 and C_2=(8/3)tau_+J_++C_* work for d>=d_*. Enlarge C_2 by (4/3)tau_+J_+d_* to cover 1<=d<d_*.
supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: L, J, tau, lambda range, open hopping model and nonnegative density coefficients. Acquired: exact one-body spectrum, canonical free-sector representation, min-max comparison and tail summation. No oracle or measured data.
cost: D-symbol classical sector map stores ceil(log2 D) bits. With cutoff d=D-1, overflow probability is Pr(M>=d); for target epsilon, D=O((1+log(1/epsilon))^(1/3)) symbols at fixed public constants, hence O(log log(1/epsilon)) stored bits. Measurement, circuit time, classical aggregation time, energy and hardware costs are not included.
error_convention: For 2<=D<=L, the exact parameter-independent map records M=0,...,D-2 and an overflow flag for M>=D-1; overflow probability is the stated error. If overflow is decoded to a fixed M value, the induced M-marginal TV error is at most the overflow probability. At D=L+1, map all M=0,...,L exactly with no overflow. The map discards within-sector quantum information and is not a whole-state trace-norm archive.
strongest_comparator: Exact unnormalized sector-by-sector canonical trace domination Z_M(W)<=Z_M(0), followed by the vacuum lower bound Z>=1 and the parameter-matched free XX canonical partition tail. Normalized stochastic domination of the free M distribution is not asserted because normalizers differ.
falsifier: Any allowed positive number-preserving W violating the explicit finite-L tail inequality would falsify the claim. The proof rules this out under the listed assumptions. Attractive/indefinite interactions, number-changing terms, unbounded field scaling and different kinetic normalization are outside scope.
unresolved_gate: The parent programme must choose whether it seeks only the classical sector statistic or a full quantum-state archive; this result proves only the former. Independent proof review and archive novelty/priority remain open. Open/nonuniform and many-body range-R nonintegrability are not covered by the cited periodic pairwise theorem.

claim: For the periodic, shift-invariant, inversion-symmetric pairwise spin chain with nonzero NNN ZZ and nonzero NN XX exchange, Shiraishi (2025) Theorem 6 excludes k-support conserved quantities for 4<=k<=L/2 in its defined sense. The uniform t-V-V' model with nonzero NN hopping and V'>0 maps into this rank-one case after Jordan-Wigner, with a uniform longitudinal field and scalar terms. This does not cover open-edge, site-dependent, or multi-body finite-range interactions.
scope: Primary source checked at arXiv:2501.15506 v3 (2026-04-10) and Journal of Statistical Physics version published 2025-11-25. This is a scoped literature report; the source proof was not independently reconstructed here. Earlier Rabson-Narozhny-Millis (2004) level-statistics evidence is finite-size numerical and explicitly leaves thermodynamic scaling uncertain.
